newsitem.title: USA: Fed interest rate stance appropriate - U.S. lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: Fed interest rate stance appropriate - U.S. lawmaker.

text.p: The combination of moderate inflation and low unemployment in the U.S. economy suggests that there is no imminent need to raise interest rates, the chairman of Congress' Joint Economic Committee said on Friday.
"I believe that the Federal Reserve has recently adopted an appropriate stance," chairman Jim Saxton, a Republican of New Jersey, said at a committee hearing on the employment situation.

"Rather than overreacting to healthy real economic and employment growth and low unemployment, monetary policy is consistent with the view that other variables are more reliable indicators of future inflation," he added.
Saxton quoted indicators such as commodity prices, the value of the dollar and bond yields as suggesting that "no serious upturn in inflation is imminent."

The U.S. central bank's Federal Open Market Committee last raised short-term interest rates by a quarter percentage point on March 25. It opted to keep rates steady at its subsequent meetings on May 20 and July 1-2.
The government earlier on Thursday reported that the July unemployment rate dropped to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June.
